headline: High: OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/REST surfaces can ingest EMQX-fed content, creating default-path prompt injection, data leakage, and compliance risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: EMQX exposes an HTTP API and broad network egress, while OpenBBTerminal can consume MCP servers and REST APIs. That creates a plausible bridge where EMQX-originated content reaches OpenBBTerminal as tool input. The profiles do not prove direct instruction parsing, so I do not escalate to high, but the shared channel exists in default-capable configurations.
conditions: IF EMQX-delivered payloads are forwarded into OpenBBTerminal MCP or REST inputs without provenance filtering, injection is possible.
IF OpenBBTerminal treats API-returned text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all EMQX-fed messages before OpenBBTerminal ingests them.
Disable automatic tool execution on OpenBBTerminal inputs.
Restrict OpenBBTerminal to allowlisted MCP servers only.
Review one sample end-to-end payload path for instruction-like text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and schema validation at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress; OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and can call MCP/REST APIs. If they share a workspace or relay data through APIs, sensitive data can cross boundaries. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, so this is not high, but the default-capable API bridge makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF IoT data from EMQX is forwarded into OpenBBTerminal queries or logs, cross-domain leakage occurs.
IF OpenBBTerminal sends API payloads containing financial or licensed data to external services, those data classes can leak beyond the intended boundary.
mitigations: Minimize fields forwarded from EMQX to OpenBBTerminal.
Turn off verbose logging on both sides.
Separate credentials and API keys per agent.
Inspect one sample request/response pair for sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace and network segmentation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has broad network egress and HTTP API access, while OpenBBTerminal can use MCP/REST APIs but cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. The overlap is mainly read/network interaction rather than competing writes, so conflict risk is limited. No shared mutable resource is documented, so I keep this low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external API quota or rate-limited endpoint, request contention can occur.
IF an operator manually shares a single credential across both agents, one agent can starve the other.
mitigations: Use separate API credentials for each agent.
Set per-agent rate limits.
Stagger scheduled runs by a few minutes.
Monitor 429/timeout errors for contention.
requires-engineering: add a lock or queue around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal’s sandboxing says 'connect once, consume everywhere,' and it supports MCP/REST inputs, so it may treat upstream outputs as authoritative. EMQX can emit networked API content, creating a plausible chain where EMQX-derived data is rendered or acted on by OpenBBTerminal without verification. The profiles do not prove automation to emails or commits, so medium is the highest supported level.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes EMQX output as a market or operational signal without validation, downstream decisions can be wrong.
IF an operator wires EMQX output directly into OpenBBTerminal workflows, errors can cascade across multiple work products.
mitigations: Require a human review step before acting on EMQX-fed outputs.
Compare EMQX-derived values against a second source.
Label upstream data as untrusted in OpenBBTerminal.
Sample one workflow for missing validation checks.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection rules.

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and has broad network/API surfaces. The pair therefore creates a realistic compliance-breach pathway if regulated or licensed data is routed through the wrong agent or logging path. Because the profiles do not show residency or certification controls, uncertainty pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated IoT telemetry or financial data is routed through the other agent’s logs or APIs, policy mismatch can occur.
IF OpenBBTerminal processes licensed data outside its permitted terms, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents.
Disable retention of sensitive logs where possible.
Keep licensed data out of EMQX-fed workflows.
Review one data-flow diagram for residency and retention gaps.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls.
